html:
Cumbia is a music and dance from the Caribbean coast of Colombia, joining African drums, Indigenous flutes and Spanish song. From the 1940s it spread from the coast to the whole country and then across Latin America.

It grew from the music of Afro-Colombian and Indigenous communities near Cartagena and the Magdalena River, played on drums and gaitas, long cane flutes. In the 1940s and 1950s big bands from Barranquilla and Medellín brought it to dance halls and radio, and record companies sold it across the continent.

Each country made its own cumbia, from Mexico to Peru and Argentina, where it became the music of the poor neighbourhoods. With vallenato and the novels of García Márquez, cumbia made the culture of the Caribbean coast central to the image of Colombia, as tango did for Buenos Aires.
sum: Cumbia is a music and dance from the Caribbean coast of Colombia, joining African drums, Indigenous flutes and Spanish song. From the 1940s it spread from the coast to the whole country and then across Latin America.
